evidence.observed: Homebrew ffmpeg 8.1_1, built --enable-gpl --enable-version3; -L prints 'GNU General Public License ... version 3, or (at your option) any later version'.

rows.note: ONE DATED OBSERVATION OF ONE MACHINE, NEVER A LOOKUP. There is not one ffmpeg on a machine: on this one, PATH is 8.1/GPL-3/481 filters while imageio-ffmpeg's bundled binary is 7.1/GPL-2/484, and the filter sets are non-nested. Resolve a caller's ffmpeg with looks.licence.ffmpeg_terms(env) from a probe of the binary they will actually run. An LGPL build of the same source is WEAK_COPYLEFT.

rows.contradiction: av 16.0.1 states three incompatible things about itself: distribution metadata says BSD-3-Clause; the bundled avcodec_license() says 'LGPL version 3 or later'; and otool -L shows libx264.165 and libx265.215 (both GPL) actually linked into libavcodec. Its build patches FFmpeg's configure to move libx264/libx265 out of EXTERNAL_LIBRARY_GPL_LIST, so unpatched configure cannot produce that combination at all.

evidence.observed: License-Expression: BSD-3-Clause; avcodec_license() = 'LGPL version 3 or later'; configuration carries --enable-libx264 --enable-libx265 with NO --enable-gpl; libavcodec links @loader_path/libx264.165.dylib (1,691,168 B) and libx265.215.dylib (6,397,088 B); both encoders construct.

rows.note: REFUSED AS UNKNOWN, NOT AS GPL. looks does not adjudicate: it observes that the artifact's own statements disagree and declines to decide which is true. Were the contradiction resolved toward GPL, the coupling (in_process) would put it in the FORBIDDEN region, which no ceiling reaches — so the two readings differ in remedy, not in outcome. Forbidden as a looks dependency either way.

evidence.observed: imageio-ffmpeg 0.6.0 ships binaries/ffmpeg-macos-aarch64-v7.1 (49.368728 MB) built --enable-gpl --enable-libx264 --enable-libx265; -L prints GPL v2 or later. Distribution metadata says BSD-2-Clause.

rows.note: The metadata field says BSD-2-Clause and the shipped executable is GPL-2.0-or-later. This row is why looks never reads a licence from metadata. Forbidden as a looks dependency (zero-dependency non-negotiable); the row exists to explain the refusal and to classify a caller's pre-existing install.

rows.note: Why looks -> burns is forbidden while burns -> looks is fine: pip install burns puts a GPL binary on disk, and looks declares stdlib only. The dependency edge runs one way for a licence reason, not a taste one.

evidence.observed: cv2.pyrMeanShiftFiltering is OpenCV main-module C++ under Apache-2.0; it never enters libavcodec.

rows.note: The flatten stage of the Que Calor chain, as CODE. Permissive on its own; every wheel row below is a separate component, and the worst one wins.

evidence.command: strings on the shipped libavutil; ls cv2/.dylibs; vmmap on a process that only did `import cv2`
evidence.observed: The bundled ffmpeg is built --enable-gpl --enable-version3 --enable-libx264 --enable-libx265 and its avutil_license() says 'GPL version 3 or later'. `import cv2` alone maps libavcodec, libavfilter, libavformat, libavutil, libpostproc, librubberband, libvidstab, libx264.164 and libx265.215 into the live Python process, unconditionally and at import.

rows.note: COUPLING IS DELIBERATELY UNKNOWN, AND THAT IS THE ANSWER, NOT A GAP. Whether cv2's dynamic linkage of its bundled GPL libavcodec counts as looks' own in-process coupling is the open question in decisions section 11: read one way the row is FORBIDDEN at every ceiling, read the other it is COPYLEFT_SHIPPED and merely above the default. That adjudication is exactly what the honesty rule forbids looks from making, so this row refuses as UNKNOWN. Section 5.7's Tier column records COPYLEFT_SHIPPED; the two readings are indistinguishable under the default ceiling and differ only at max_tier=COPYLEFT_SHIPPED. Settle it with the owner, or make it moot: -DWITH_FFMPEG=OFF, a non-OpenCV mean-shift, or an ffmpeg-native flattener.

evidence.observed: NO LICENSE FILE. The GitHub API returns license: null. The README prose says the work is 'made freely available to academic and non-academic entities for non-commercial purposes' and that commercial use requires a written authorisation letter.

conditions: Share-alike: an adapted work must be distributed under the same terms.

evidence.observed: README: 'Licensed under the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license'; 'Commercial application is prohibited'. There is no LICENSE file.

rows.note: A LISTED SPDX id whose non-commercial character is NOT derivable from the id string, which is why field_of_use is a declared column and never parsed. Reach is left underived on purpose: CC BY-NC-SA's share-alike attaches to an adapted work, and mapping that onto a software copyleft reach would be an adjudication. So the row is field-restricted with no rung, and even a caller who opts into NON_COMMERCIAL is refused at the ceiling test for want of a tier.

A clean licence is necessary, not sufficient.

evidence.observed: The repository releases the implementation into the public domain. It implements Adobe's PatchMatch, US8861869B2, which Google Patents reports Active with an anticipated expiry of 2030-08-16.

rows.note: REACH IS RECORDED EXPLICITLY because 'public domain' has no SPDX id here. This row is the whole argument for a patent field: public-domain is the most permissive value any copyright vocabulary has, and for this artifact it is the wrong answer. looks records the patent and reports it as an advisory; it does not refuse on it, because a patent binds an act in a jurisdiction rather than a redistribution, and deciding whether it binds YOUR act is the adjudication the honesty rule forbids.

rows.note: Derives WEAK_COPYLEFT, where section 5.7's Tier column reads 'COPYLEFT_SHIPPED if vendored'. The conflict is flagged rather than resolved silently: section 5.3's ladder lifts a rung for conveyance ONLY inside the strong-copyleft subprocess region, and section 5.7 itself contains the contrary row (the manylinux headless wheel, an LGPL library that is equally conveyed, tiered WEAK_COPYLEFT). Two rows of one table cannot both be right under one projection, so looks follows the decided ladder. Either way, conveying an LGPL work is a real source-offer duty on the work itself.

rows.prohibition: The model card excludes the EU, the UK, South Korea and the USA by territory. For a US or EU caller there is no grant at all, so no ceiling and no field-of-use opt-in reaches it.

Read this row's verdict as 'for a US/EU caller' — the exclusion is about who you are, and looks records the observation rather than your jurisdiction.
